AlertKind.description:
Every cause that can raise an alert (SPEC §10.3).

SPEC §3.1 says "24 values"; §10.3's table groups the three
``permission_lost_*`` causes on one line and pairs
``retention_job_failed``/``backup_failed`` on another. Expanded, the closed
set is the 27 below — the count in §3.1 is a count of table rows.
AlertKind.title: AlertKind

AlertResponse.description: One open or acknowledged alert, as the inbox renders it.

body_uz.description: What to do about it. Derived from `kind`, not stored.

installation_status.description: Status of the installation this alert is about. New alerts are not raised against a superseded phone and its open ones are closed when it is replaced — this is here so a page can also tell at a glance, without a second query, for alerts raised before that rule existed.

occurrence_count.description: Repeats bump this rather than inserting a row: a phone reporting every two minutes must not produce 720 rows a day.

title_uz.description: What happened, in Uzbek. Derived from `kind`, not stored.

AlertResponse.title: AlertResponse

AppVariant.description:
The ``targetSdk`` product flavour (D-06).

Reported on every heartbeat, stored on every call, so capture rate is
measurable per variant and not only per handset model.
AppVariant.title: AppVariant

signing_sha256_configured.description: Whether a signing fingerprint is configured. False means uploads are accepted without the key check — see docs/APK-SIGNING.md.

AppVersionResponse.description: One build in the distribution record.

created_by_name.description: Who uploaded it, resolved server-side. The id alone would make every page re-solve it through `GET /users`, which a manager cannot read — so a manager would see a bare uuid.

published_at.description: NULL means uploaded but not published — reaches nobody.

AppVersionResponse.title: AppVersionResponse

AssignmentListResponse.description: Full history for a number — this is the timeline the agent page renders.
AssignmentListResponse.title: AssignmentListResponse

AttestRequest.description:
``POST /api/v1/installations/{id}/attest`` (T142).

Attestation is deliberately weaker evidence than a proven binding, and the
reason is mandatory: an unexplained attestation is indistinguishable from a
mistake six months later.
AttestRequest.title: AttestRequest

AudioMissingReason.description:
Why a call has no audio. Closed, ``NOT NULL`` whenever audio is absent (N5).

UC-14 names six; SPEC §3.9 justifies the other four one by one. The gap
report's denominator excludes ``pending_upload`` and ``not_expected``,
which is what keeps "% of answered calls with audio" honest.
AudioMissingReason.title: AudioMissingReason

AuditAction.description:
Every auditable action (UC-24, N27).

SPEC §3.16 was written against this set after the fact and added two values
to it. Both earn their place by being separately *filterable*:

* ``retention_changed`` is technically a ``setting_updated``, but it is the
  one setting whose change destroys data — "who shortened retention, and
  when" must be one filter, not a JSONB dig through every settings change.
* ``command_issued`` is a person reaching into an employee's **personally
  owned** phone. It is the only action in the product that acts on somebody
  else's hardware, and this log is the only place that is visible.

Adding a value is a migration, which is the point: the list is closed so
that "everything that happened" is answerable from one column.
AuditAction.title: AuditAction

AuditResponse.description: One thing that happened. Immutable, by database trigger.

detail.description: Before/after values and counts. Never a password, a token or an enrolment code (N26). Open by nature — this is a server-side record, not a device payload, so §8's allow-list does not apply.

AuditResponse.title: AuditResponse

CallAudioSummary.description:
What the call list and the detail page need to know about the audio.

``capture_route`` is here and not folded into "audio: yes/no" because
``S1-RECORDING.md`` is explicit that ``app_voice_recognition`` and
``app_mic`` must stay distinguishable: the per-model capture rate is the M0
baseline, and UC-23's regression alert compares against it. Collapsing the
routes would make "which mechanism actually works on this handset" an
unanswerable question.

available.description: Playable now — stored and not yet expired.

capture_route.description: Which strategy produced it (S1, M0, UC-23).

capture_route_detail.description: The folder name only, never a path from the phone.

duration_mismatch.description: The file's length disagrees with the call log (UC-14).

url.description: Path to stream from, present only when the recording is available. A path and never a signed or public URL (N20): the endpoint is token-protected, and the panel reaches it through the Service Worker bridge because a plain <audio src> cannot send an Authorization header (T153, N43).

CallAudioSummary.title: CallAudioSummary

CallDirection.description:
Ours, not BonviZvonki's ``inbound``/``outbound``.

The export (SPEC §4.9) maps ours onto theirs in exactly one place, so the
two vocabularies never leak into each other.
CallDirection.title: CallDirection

CallDisposition.description:
UC-11's five classes are direction x disposition.

``missed`` and ``rejected`` are incoming-only, ``no_answer`` is
outgoing-only — enforced by a CHECK, so the invalid combinations are
unrepresentable rather than merely unused.
CallDisposition.title: CallDisposition

CallListResponse.description:
A cursor page of calls (SPEC §4.0).

``total`` is computed only when the caller asks: a COUNT(*) over a filtered
500k table is affordable once per filter change and not once per page.
CallListResponse.title: CallListResponse

CallResponse.description:
A call as the panel reads it.

Carries the display fields, not only ids. Making the browser look up an
agent's name per row is the N+1 problem relocated to the client, and the
``device_model`` filter would otherwise exist server-side for a column the
panel cannot show.

agent_name.description: Resolved server-side; the panel renders it.

device_model.description: 'Xiaomi Redmi Note 12'. The device_model filter needs it.

number_e164.description: The registered line the call happened on.

CallResponse.title: CallResponse

CallType.description:
Internal vs external (UC-25). ``unknown`` is the mandatory default.

An empty line directory yields ``unknown``, never ``external``:
BonviZvonki defaulted to external and 82 of 98 calls were mislabelled.
CallType.title: CallType

Capability.description:
One row per installation per capability (UC-03, §7.8).

Every one of these is verified by exercising it, never by reading a
permission flag — that is what makes ``granted_not_working`` expressible.
Capability.title: Capability

CapabilityState.description: ``granted_not_working`` is the OEM-permission-manager case UC-03 names.
CapabilityState.title: CapabilityState

CapabilityStateResponse.description:
One capability's current state, as the panel's matrix renders it.

A **required** capability the phone has never reported appears here as
``unknown`` with null timestamps, rather than being absent. Absence made
the page show every row green while ``capturing`` was false, with nothing
on screen saying which capability was missing — and a phone stuck part-way
through E2 is exactly that shape.

changed_at.description: Null until there is a state to have changed from.

checked_at.description: Null when this capability has never been checked.

CapabilityStateResponse.title: CapabilityStateResponse

CaptureRoute.description:
Which mechanism produced the recording (S1, the M0 baseline).

``NONE`` may only appear with ``has_audio = false``.
CaptureRoute.title: CaptureRoute

new_password.description: Minimum 10 characters and no other composition rule (SPEC §4.7): a rule people cannot follow is a rule they write on a sticky note.

CommandFailureReason.description: Why a command did not happen. UC-16 requires the panel to say which.
CommandFailureReason.title: CommandFailureReason

CommandKind.description: Server-to-device commands. No ``send_sms`` — SMS is out of scope.
CommandKind.title: CommandKind

latency_ms.description: acked_at - created_at, stored so UC-16's five-second bar is **measured** rather than assumed. R3 flags that bar as possibly unachievable on doze-restricted OEMs; this column is what turns that into a conversation with evidence.

CreateAgentRequest.description: ``POST /api/v1/agents``. Creating an agent never creates a login.

employee_code.description: The roster import key; unique where set.

CreateAgentRequest.title: CreateAgentRequest

CreateAssignmentRequest.description: ``POST /api/v1/numbers/{id}/assignments`` — hand a line to an agent.

valid_from.description: Defaults to now. The period is [valid_from, valid_to).

valid_to.description: NULL means open-ended — they hold it now.

CreateAssignmentRequest.title: CreateAssignmentRequest

number.description: For kind='dial'. Named, not a free-form payload map (§8).

pattern.description: Digits to match. UC-25's '*700' is the suffix rule '700'.

CreateNumberRequest.description:
``POST /api/v1/numbers``.

The number is normalised to E.164 before it is stored, so the same line
typed three ways is one row — the uniqueness lives on the generated
``phone_key`` column, not on this string.

operator.description: beeline | ucell | mobiuz | uzmobile | other. A reporting axis (R19).

sim_owner.description: R10: which SIM relationships are not Bonvi's to keep.

CreateNumberRequest.title: CreateNumberRequest

agent_id.description: Required when role='sales' — it is what own-scope narrowing filters on, and the database has a CHECK saying so.

CurrentUserResponse.description:
``GET /api/v1/auth/me`` — what the panel's ``can()`` reads.

The permission list is resolved server-side and sent whole. The panel never
holds a role-to-permission map: a second copy of the matrix is a second
thing to forget to update.

agent_id.description: Set for a 'sales' account; what own-scope filters on.

must_change_password.description: The panel forces the change before anything else loads.

CurrentUserResponse.title: CurrentUserResponse

DataUsageRowOut.description: One installation's traffic against the cap the employee pays for.

over_cap.description: Past N14's cap: the app stops uploading audio over cellular.

DataUsageRowOut.title: DataUsageRowOut

DeviceDetailResponse.description: Device health plus its capability matrix (UC-17's device page).

bound_at.description: When this installation was bound to the number.

capabilities.description: Empty for a phone that has never reported — not missing.

capturing.description: UC-03's never-false-ready rule: every required capability working, a verified installation and a live service. One function computes it, so the phone and the panel cannot disagree.

created_at.description: When the row was created. With `installation_status` it is what distinguishes a live binding from one superseded an hour ago.

is_online.description: Derived, never stored: last_heartbeat_at is inside the alerts.device_offline_minutes window. Storing it would need a job to keep it false, and it would be wrong between runs.

never_reported.description: Bound and never sent a heartbeat. Kept distinct from ``is_online: false`` because the next action differs: never started is a person waiting for help right now; worked once and stopped is a phone in a lift or a battery manager to argue with.

ws_connected.description: Shown separately from is_online on purpose: a socket can be alive while capture is dead, and conflating the two is how a broken phone looks fine.

DeviceDetailResponse.title: DeviceDetailResponse

DeviceHealthResponse.description: Every UC-17 field, plus the identity the panel needs to name a person.

bound_at.description: When this installation was bound to the number.

capturing.description: Whether this phone is recording **right now**: every required capability working, the installation verified, the service alive (UC-03). Never null — a phone that has told us nothing is not recording, and a null here reads as 'no problem' to any check asking whether it is false.

created_at.description: When the row was created. With `installation_status` it is what distinguishes a live binding from one superseded an hour ago.

is_online.description: Derived, never stored: last_heartbeat_at is inside the alerts.device_offline_minutes window. Storing it would need a job to keep it false, and it would be wrong between runs.

never_reported.description: Bound and never sent a heartbeat. Kept distinct from ``is_online: false`` because the next action differs: never started is a person waiting for help right now; worked once and stopped is a phone in a lift or a battery manager to argue with.

ws_connected.description: Shown separately from is_online on purpose: a socket can be alive while capture is dead, and conflating the two is how a broken phone looks fine.

DeviceHealthResponse.title: DeviceHealthResponse

EnrolmentAttemptKind.description: ``step_timing`` carries the per-screen durations that make N40 measurable.
EnrolmentAttemptKind.title: EnrolmentAttemptKind

EnrolmentAttemptResponse.description: Where UC-01's failures appear, with timestamps.
EnrolmentAttemptResponse.title: EnrolmentAttemptResponse

EnrolmentCodeResponse.description: The code plus everything the admin has to pass on.
EnrolmentCodeResponse.title: EnrolmentCodeResponse

EnrolmentOutcome.description: Every way an enrolment step can end. The funnel's evidence base.
EnrolmentOutcome.title: EnrolmentOutcome

ErrorBody.description:
The body of every non-2xx answer (N35, SPEC §4.0).

A model rather than a fragment hand-written in the exporter, so the shape
clients generate against is the shape ``main.error_envelope`` builds.
``tests/test_conformance.py`` drives real requests through both.

code.description: The stable machine value. Clients branch on this.

message.description: Uzbek, for a person. Never branched on (§4.0).

request_id.description: Echoed from X-Request-Id; quote it in a bug report.

ErrorBody.title: ErrorBody

ErrorResponse.description: ``{"error": {...}}`` — the envelope itself, and the only error shape.
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

FunnelStage.description:
Where an agent is in the rollout (UC-17, SPEC §10.1).

``verified_by_admin`` is visibly distinct from ``number_verified`` because
attested is weaker evidence than proven, and the identity anchor must never
degrade silently (T142).
FunnelStage.title: FunnelStage

api_level.description: Part of the M0 baseline's identity.

app_variant.description: Capture rate is per variant, not only per model (D-06).

delta_pp.description: Below the threshold raises N4's alert.

GapByReasonOut.description: Why audio is missing, and how often. The closed enum, never free text.

counts_against_capture_rate.description: ``pending_upload`` and ``not_expected`` are excluded from the denominator: an unanswered call in it makes '% of answered calls with audio' meaningless (SPEC §3.9).

GapByReasonOut.title: GapByReasonOut

missing_total.description: Matches the filtered call list, because the same rows are counted.

status.description: Always 'ok' when the process is serving.

ImportAgentsRequest.description:
``POST /api/v1/agents/import`` — CSV text, not a file upload.

A one-off for ~33 people (T59), not a live integration. Text rather than a
multipart file because the realistic input is a paste out of a spreadsheet,
and asking somebody to save a file first is a step that fails.

dry_run.description: Default true, deliberately: the diff is shown before anything is written, because a roster import that half-succeeded is worse than one that did not run.

ImportAgentsRequest.title: ImportAgentsRequest

ImportRowResult.description: What would happen, or did happen, to one roster line.

reason.description: Why it was skipped or refused.

ImportRowResult.title: ImportRowResult

InstallationResponse.description: One installation, as the panel reads it.
InstallationResponse.title: InstallationResponse

InstallationStatus.description: Lifecycle of one app installation bound to one registered number.
InstallationStatus.title: InstallationStatus

LoginResponse.description: The user *and* their access token, so the panel needs one round trip.

agent_id.description: Set for a 'sales' account; what own-scope filters on.

must_change_password.description: The panel forces the change before anything else loads.

LoginResponse.title: LoginResponse

phone_key.description: Last 9 digits, generated by the database (N37).

OpenDeltaOut.description: A device whose own call-log count never reconciled (N3, §4.1 B).

subscription_unknown_count.description: Never folded into either side of the rate — the fail-closed rule made visible.

OpenDeltaOut.title: OpenDeltaOut

ReadyResponse.description: Dependency readiness, one flag per dependency.

storage.description: The audio root exists and is writable.

ReadyResponse.title: ReadyResponse

ReceiverStatus.description: No heartbeat for 3 min -> degraded, 5 min -> down + a critical alert.
ReceiverStatus.title: ReceiverStatus

ReceiverStatusResponse.description:
The banner at the top of the rollout page (SPEC §9.4).

**If every receiver is down, nobody in the fleet can enrol**, so this is
the page's most important sentence and it says so before anyone tries. It
carries a real type for the same reason: an untyped body reaches the
contract as a free-form map, and the panel then has to parse defensively
exactly where it can least afford to guess.

active_receivers.description: More than one is a configuration change, not code.

enrolment_possible.description: False means the rollout is stopped, not slow.

receiver_msisdn.description: The number screen E5 shows the agent.

receiver_name.description: Which gateway, for the admin to go and look at.

status.description: up | degraded | down. Down is 5 minutes without a heartbeat.

ReceiverStatusResponse.title: ReceiverStatusResponse

ReclassifyResponse.description: A directory change is only half done until the calls agree with it.

calls_reclassified.description: Calls whose call_type changed as a result of this edit.

ReclassifyResponse.title: ReclassifyResponse

RevokeResponse.description:
What was still queued when contact was lost.

Bonvi does not own the handset, so a revoke that claims a completed wipe
would be lying. ``revoke_confirmed_at`` stays NULL until the phone comes
back and says the local audio is gone.
RevokeResponse.title: RevokeResponse

SetMinimumVersionRequest.description:
``PUT /api/v1/app/min-version``.

``acknowledged_stranded`` must equal the count the impact endpoint returns
right now. Not ceremony: it fails exactly when the number moved between
looking and deciding, which is when the admin's picture is stale.

acknowledged_stranded.description: The stranded count you just saw. Must still be true.

SetMinimumVersionRequest.title: SetMinimumVersionRequest

StoragePointOut.description: One day of the growth curve.
StoragePointOut.title: StoragePointOut

StorageReportResponse.description: N18: current usage, 30-day growth, and the projection it implies.

projected_bytes_12m.description: Today's total plus a year at the last 30 days' rate. The provision is 250 GB, and this is what says whether that is enough.

StorageReportResponse.title: StorageReportResponse

StrandedInstallationOut.description: One phone a proposed minimum version would refuse.
StrandedInstallationOut.title: StrandedInstallationOut

UpdateNumberRequest.description: ``PATCH /api/v1/numbers/{id}``. The number itself is not editable.
UpdateNumberRequest.title: UpdateNumberRequest

UpdateSettingRequest.description:
``PUT /api/v1/settings``.

``confirm`` exists for one case: lowering the retention period below
``retention.confirm_below_months`` destroys recordings that still exist.
Without it the server changes nothing and returns 409 (SPEC §3.11).

confirm.description: Required when the change would delete data that still exists.

UpdateSettingRequest.title: UpdateSettingRequest

UpdateUserRequest.description: ``PATCH /api/v1/users/{id}``. Every field optional; absent means unchanged.
UpdateUserRequest.title: UpdateUserRequest

UploadReleaseResponse.description: What the upload found in the file, alongside the row it created.

signer_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the signing certificate, read from the APK's v2/v3 signing block. Compare it against docs/APK-SIGNING.md by eye if no fingerprint is configured yet — a build signed by another key cannot be installed as an update, only as an uninstall that destroys the phone's unsent queue.

signer_verified.description: True when it was checked against the configured fingerprint.

UploadReleaseResponse.title: UploadReleaseResponse

UserListResponse.description: A page of accounts. Small table, so no cursor: the panel shows them all.
UserListResponse.title: UserListResponse

UserResponse.description: A panel account. Never carries the hash.
UserResponse.title: UserResponse

UserRole.description:
A panel login's role (SPEC §3.2).

``service`` is deliberately absent: machine access is a ``service_tokens``
row, because a machine has no password, no session and no navigation. The
authorisation registry in ``core/permissions.py`` covers both and a test
asserts these three are a subset of it.

``viewer`` was removed on 2026-09-05 with the TV board — see
``core.permissions.Role``.
UserRole.title: UserRole

VerificationMethod.description:
How we proved the phone holds the registered number (UC-04, T142).

Ordered strongest to weakest, and the order is load-bearing: SPEC §9.3
requires the identity anchor to degrade visibly, so every place that
renders a binding renders which of these it rests on.

``self_declared`` is the weakest. It says only that whoever held the
single-use code an admin issued for this number typed it into this handset
— no line was proven. It exists because on this fleet the two proving
routes are frequently both unavailable: Uzbek SIMs leave
``getLine1Number()`` empty, and the callback route needs a receiver line.
Without it those handsets have no path to ``active`` at all, which is
strictly worse: an unenrolled phone reports nothing, so nobody can even see
that it is unverified. Governed by ``enrolment.allow_self_declared``.
VerificationMethod.title: VerificationMethod

VersionGateImpactResponse.description:
What raising the floor would cost, **before** it is raised (N34, UC-28).

These are personally owned handsets. A stranded phone drains its queue,
is then refused, and stays refused until somebody physically reaches that
salesperson — so this is not a preview of a config change, it is the cost
of a decision, and the panel shows it before the button.

unknown_version_count.description: Active phones that have never reported a version code. The gate lets these through, so they are not counted as stranded — but each one might be below the floor and we cannot say.

VersionGateImpactResponse.title: VersionGateImpactResponse

get.description:
A cursor page. Default and guaranteed-stable sort is ``received_at DESC``.

Keyset, not offset: no row that existed when paging started is skipped or
returned twice, which is what UC-19 asks for and what an OFFSET cannot give
while calls keep arriving. **Every sort pairs with ``id``**, or paging
duplicates the rows whose sort values tie — and duration ties constantly.

get.description:
Streaming CSV for the same filter as the list (T48, UC-22).

UTF-8 **with a BOM** and a ``;`` delimiter: Excel in a ru/uz locale renders
a comma-separated UTF-8 file as one column, and the person who opens it has
no way to know that is what happened.

A ``sales`` export is own-rows-only and carries no other agent's name,
because the same scoped query builds it.

422.description: Validation error, in the standard envelope

delete.description:
**405 for every role, including admin** (UC-26, T45).

The route exists precisely so that the refusal is explicit and testable.
Without it a DELETE would 405 from the router with FastAPI's own body, and
"nobody can delete a call" would be an absence rather than a decision.
Only the retention job removes audio, and it never removes a call.

**No permission dependency on purpose.** T45 asserts 405 for all five
roles, so the refusal has to outrank authorisation: a role that cannot read
calls getting 403 here would mean the answer depends on who is asking, and
it does not.
A caller with no token still gets 401 — that is the principal dependency.
